title: Files: make, copy, move, delete
summary: mkdir, touch, cp, mv and rm: the everyday moves, and the one that has no undo.

text: - mkdir makes a folder. mkdir -p a/b/c makes the whole chain at once.
- touch makes an empty file (or updates the date of one that exists).
- mv moves, and renaming is just moving to a new name.
- Copying a folder needs -r (recursive): cp -r notes backup.
rm deletes for good. There is no recycle bin on the command line.
- rm -r deletes a folder and everything inside: read the line twice first.
- rm -i asks before each file, a good habit while you learn.
